newsitem.title: USA: FAA proposes Airbus 600's be inspected more often.
newsitem.headline: FAA proposes Airbus 600's be inspected more often.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration has proposed a new airworthiness directive to require more frequent inspections to prevent cracking in Airbus model A300-600 series planes.
The FAA proposal, published in the Federal Register Wednesday, would lower the threshold of the number of landings and flight hours required for the inspections.

The action was prompted by notification by Airbus that there were reports of cracks appearing in the angles of the wings on planes that had fewer landings and flight hours than were covered by an earlier airworthiness directive. Airbus reported that the airplanes on which this cracking had been detected had accumulated between 5,540 and 21,200 landings and between 11,616 and 21,250 flight hours.
The FAA said its proposal would cost about $480 per airplane. The agency said 34 Model A300-600 series Airbus planes are registered in the United States.
The FAA will consider comments received by July 28.
